addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Pattern Consolidation Plan
2	
3	This plan adds a pattern layer to Entire Brain: the brain notices repeated repository work, summarizes it with retained evidence, and forms selected patterns into reusable agent skills.
4	
5	The design keeps the public surface small and task-oriented. Internal terms should support the brain metaphor without leaking implementation details into the user workflow.
6	
7	## Vocabulary
8	
9	| Term | Meaning |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Episode | One user request, the agent work that followed, and the next user feedback signal. |
12	| Procedure | A repeated command, tool, file, or validation workflow. |
13	| Practice | A repeated judgment, review, diagnosis, or model-steering behavior. |
14	| Pattern | A recurring procedure or practice. |
15	| Reinforcement | User approval, correction, commit/checkpoint success, or other feedback. |
16	| Consolidation | The process of turning a recurring pattern into a durable skill candidate. |
17	| Pattern card | Evidence summary shown to the user before skill creation or update. |
18	| Skill memory | Registry of patterns already accepted, declined, or needing update. |
19	| Synapse | Internal-only weighted edge connecting episodes, facts, procedures, symbols, outcomes, and pattern evidence. |
20	
21	Avoid anatomical CLI names. User-facing commands should say `patterns`, `form`, `status`, and `refresh`; `synapse` remains an internal data model term only.
22	
23	## Goals
24	
25	- Notice repeated procedures and practices from Entire session history.
26	- Show evidence-backed pattern cards before any write.
27	- Form selected patterns into reusable skills.
28	- Track accepted, declined, and changed patterns so the brain does not repeatedly propose the same work.
29	- Treat workspace-level patterns as first-class, not as a later extension.
30	- Reuse existing brain sources: sessions, history, facts, docs, semantic graph, workspace membership, write locks, and agent runner infrastructure.
31	
32	## Non-Goals
33	
34	- Do not add developer-only CLI commands for raw episodes or synapses.
35	- Do not make the feature dependent on hosted model calls for the deterministic refresh path.
36	- Do not overwrite user-edited skill files without explicit confirmation.
37	- Do not replace durable facts, semantic graph inspection, or retrieval. Patterns are a new layer built from those sources.
38	
39	## Storage Model
40	
41	Add a `patterns` source to the brain manifest:
42	
43	```json
44	{
45	  "sources": {
46	    "patterns": {
47	      "generated_at": "2026-06-16T00:00:00Z",
48	      "episodes": 1234,
49	      "procedures": 42,
50	      "practices": 18,
51	      "patterns": 12,
52	      "skill_memory": 5,
53	      "fingerprint": "sha256:..."
54	    }
55	  }
56	}
57	```
58	
59	Persist derived data under the brain directory:
60	
61	```text
62	patterns/
63	  episodes.ndjson
64	  procedures.ndjson
65	  practices.ndjson
66	  patterns.ndjson
67	  synapses.ndjson
68	  cards/
69	    <pattern-id>.json
70	    <pattern-id>.md
71	  skill-memory.ndjson
72	```
73	
74	Use the existing brain write lock and atomic write helpers. Treat all files as derived and rebuildable except `skill-memory.ndjson`, which is user-state and must be preserved across refreshes.
75	
76	## Episode Layer
77	
78	Build episodes from exported session transcripts. An episode is the normalized unit used by pattern detection:
79	
80	```json
81	{
82	  "id": "episode:...",
83	  "repo_key": "gh/ashtom/entire-brain",
84	  "workspace": "platform",
85	  "session_id": "...",
86	  "checkpoint_id": "...",
87	  "branch": "main",
88	  "author": "Thomas Dohmke",
89	  "agent": "Codex",
90	  "intent": "review release readiness",
91	  "intent_signature": "review:release",
92	  "tool_sequence": ["search", "read", "edit", "test"],
93	  "command_sequence": ["go test ./...", "gofmt -w ."],
94	  "files": ["internal/cli/refresh.go"],
95	  "reinforcement": "success",
96	  "source": {
97	    "path": "sessions/main/...",
98	    "line": 123
99	  }
100	}
101	```
102	
103	Episode extraction should:
104	
105	- Count only actual agent tool calls and executed commands, not examples in prose.
106	- Preserve source anchors into retained transcripts.
107	- Classify reinforcement from the next user turn and available Entire checkpoint/session metadata.
108	- Keep branch, repo, author, agent, and workspace identity on every episode.
109	- Be deterministic and safe to run during `refresh`.
110	
111	## Synapse Graph
112	
113	Use synapses internally to preserve why a pattern exists:
114	
115	```json
116	{
117	  "from": "episode:abc",
118	  "to": "procedure:def",
119	  "kind": "supports",
120	  "weight": 0.82,
121	  "evidence": "sessions/main/...:123"
122	}
123	```
124	
125	Initial synapse kinds:
126	
127	- `supports`: an episode supports a procedure, practice, fact, symbol, or pattern.
128	- `reinforces`: a reinforcement signal strengthens or weakens a procedure/practice.
129	- `mentions`: an episode refers to a file, symbol, command, or fact.
130	- `varies`: a repo-specific procedure variant belongs to a workspace-level pattern.
131	- `contradicts`: a correction or later fact weakens a prior pattern interpretation.
132	
133	Do not expose synapses as commands. They are internal evidence edges used for scoring, cards, and future debugging through files/tests.
134	
135	## Pattern Detection
136	
137	Detect two pattern families.
138	
139	### Procedures
140	
141	Procedures come from repeated operational shapes:
142	
143	- command n-grams within an episode
144	- tool-sequence shapes
145	- repeated file/path clusters
146	- validation loops
147	- branch, release, review, or benchmark workflows
148	
149	### Practices
150	
151	Practices come from repeated judgment and interaction:
152	
153	- durable facts with kinds such as `preference`, `convention`, `gotcha`, `decision`, and `closed-negative`
154	- history records around validations, corrections, and reviews
155	- conversational or read-only episodes
156	- repeated user steering or verification expectations
157	
158	Each pattern receives a stable id, type, scope, strength, source anchors, supporting episodes, and variant metadata.
159	
160	Strength should include:
161	
162	```text
163	recurrence
164	+ span over time
165	+ recency
166	+ specificity
167	+ reinforcement quality
168	+ repo count
169	+ author count
170	+ branch count
171	```
172	
173	## Workspace Semantics
174	
175	Workspace support is a core design requirement.
176	
177	There are two scopes:
178	
179	| Scope | Meaning | Skill implication |
180	| --- | --- | --- |
181	| Repo | Repeats inside one repository. | Good for repo-local or repo-specific skills. |
182	| Workspace | Repeats across multiple repos in a workspace. | Strong signal for portable or team skills. |
183	
184	Pattern identity must include scope:
185	
186	```json
187	{
188	  "id": "pattern:...",
189	  "scope": "repo",
190	  "repo_key": "gh/entireio/cli",
191	  "workspace": ""
192	}
193	```
194	
195	```json
196	{
197	  "id": "pattern:...",
198	  "scope": "workspace",
199	  "repo_key": "",
200	  "workspace": "platform"
201	}
202	```
203	
204	Workspace consolidation should:
205	
206	- Load member repo brains by workspace membership.
207	- Combine repo-local episodes without copying generated brain data between repos.
208	- Notice procedures and practices that recur across repos.
209	- Preserve repo-specific variants.
210	- Reward patterns that recur across repos and authors.
211	- Render pattern cards with a repo breakdown.
212	
213	Example card section:
214	
215	```text
216	Seen in:
217	- api: 5 episodes, 3 success, 1 corrected
218	- web: 4 episodes, 2 success
219	- cli: 7 episodes, 5 success
220	
221	Common procedure:
222	...
223	
224	Repo-specific variations:
225	- api uses ...
226	- web uses ...
227	```
228	
229	## Public Commands
230	
231	Keep the public command surface aligned to user jobs.
232	
233	### Repo Commands
234	
235	```sh
236	entire brain patterns
237	entire brain patterns refresh
238	entire brain patterns status
239	entire brain patterns form <pattern-id>
240	```
241	
242	`entire brain patterns`
243	
244	Default read-only view. Shows strongest current patterns with concise evidence summaries and ids.
245	
246	Options:
247	
248	```sh
249	--json
250	--limit N
251	--type procedure|practice
252	--scope repo|workspace
253	```
254	
255	`entire brain patterns refresh`
256	
257	Rebuilds the pattern layer from current brain sources. `entire brain refresh` should run this by default after sessions, history, facts, docs, and semantic sources are current.
258	
259	Options:
260	
261	```sh
262	--force
263	--json
264	```
265	
266	`entire brain patterns status`
267	
268	Shows freshness and skill memory state:
269	
270	```text
271	patterns: current
272	episodes: 1234
273	procedures: 42
274	practices: 18
275	accepted skills: 5
276	declined patterns: 3
277	updates available: 2
278	```
279	
280	Options:
281	
282	```sh
283	--json
284	```
285	
286	`entire brain patterns form <pattern-id>`
287	
288	Shows the full pattern card, prepares a proposed `SKILL.md` draft, then asks where, if anywhere, to install it. The command must not write files until the user chooses a destination.
289	
290	Options:
291	
292	```sh
293	--name <skill-name>
294	--destination global|repo
295	--yes
296	--json
297	```
298	
299	In non-interactive mode, require both `--name` and `--yes`.
300	
301	### Workspace Commands
302	
303	Mirror the repo commands without expanding the surface:
304	
305	```sh
306	entire brain workspace patterns <workspace>
307	entire brain workspace patterns refresh <workspace>
308	entire brain workspace patterns status <workspace>
309	entire brain workspace patterns form <workspace> <pattern-id>
310	```
311	
312	Workspace `patterns` should show cross-repo patterns by default and include repo breakdowns in each card.
313	
314	## Pattern Cards
315	
316	A pattern card is the approval surface for skill creation or update.
317	
318	Card shape:
319	
320	```text
321	Pattern: release-readiness-evidence
322	Type: procedure
323	Scope: workspace
324	Strength: high
325	Reinforcement: 12 success, 2 corrected, 9 neutral
326	Seen in: 8 sessions, 3 repos, 2 authors
327	
328	What repeats:
329	...
330	
331	Trigger:
332	Use when ...
333	
334	Evidence:
335	- session/checkpoint/path:line
336	- real command/tool sequence
337	- supporting fact ids
338	
339	Would become:
340	- Steps
341	- Verification
342	- Failure modes
343	```
344	
345	Rules:
346	
347	- Always show a card before asking the user to form or update a skill.
348	- Include retained source anchors.
349	- Include corrections and failure modes when available.
350	- Distinguish common workflow from repo-specific variants.
351	- Do not include raw transcripts or secrets.
352	
353	## Skill Memory
354	
355	Track user decisions in `patterns/skill-memory.ndjson`:
356	
357	```json
358	{
359	  "pattern_id": "pattern:...",
360	  "scope": "repo",
361	  "status": "active",
362	  "skill_name": "verify-release-readiness",
363	  "skill_path": "~/.agents/skills/verify-release-readiness/SKILL.md",
364	  "fingerprint": "sha256:...",
365	  "content_sha": "sha256:...",
366	  "sessions": 8,
367	  "reinforcement": {
368	    "success": 12,
369	    "corrected": 2,
370	    "neutral": 9
371	  },
372	  "created_at": "2026-06-16T00:00:00Z",
373	  "updated_at": "2026-06-16T00:00:00Z",
374	  "note": ""
375	}
376	```
377	
378	Recommendations:
379	
380	- `active/current`: accepted skill exists and evidence has not materially changed.
381	- `active/update`: evidence changed materially; offer update.
382	- `active/edited`: skill file changed since formation; present a careful update plan.
383	- `declined/current`: suppress.
384	- `declined/reconsider`: evidence materially changed; show what changed before asking again.
385	- `missing`: skill memory points to a missing file; offer to recreate or forget.
386	
387	## Skill Formation
388	
389	`patterns form` prepares a skill draft from the selected pattern card. It writes selected skills only after the user chooses an install destination.
390	
391	Interactive flow:
392	
393	1. Render the full pattern card.
394	2. Render the proposed `SKILL.md` draft.
395	3. Ask where to install it:
396	   - Global: `~/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`
397	   - Repo-local: if a repo-local convention is implemented
398	   - Draft only: print the draft without writing
399	   - Cancel
400	4. Write only after the user chooses a write destination.
401	
402	The initial implementation may support only global install, draft-only output, and cancel. Add repo-local or workspace-local destinations after the project settles those conventions.
403	
404	Default destination:
405	
406	```text
407	~/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
408	```
409	
410	Repo-local destination:
411	
412	```text
413	<repo>/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
414	```
415	
416	If the project settles on a different repo-local convention, use that consistently and document it in `README.md`.
417	
418	Generated skill shape:
419	
420	```markdown
421	---
422	name: <name>
423	description: Use when ...
424	---
425	
426	# <Name>
427	
428	## Steps
429	
430	...
431	
432	## Verification
433	
434	...
435	
436	## Failure Modes
437	
438	...
439	
440	## Evidence
441	
442	Formed by Entire Brain from N sessions with retained source anchors.
443	```
444	
445	Skill body rules:
446	
447	- Keep steps focused on future behavior, not session recap.
448	- Include verification when evidence shows how work was checked.
449	- Include failure modes from corrections.
450	- Keep source anchors concise.
451	- Never write or overwrite a file before the destination choice is explicit.
452	- Recompute and store `content_sha` after writing.
453	
454	## Refresh Integration
455	
456	`entire brain refresh` should run pattern refresh after:
457	
458	1. sessions
459	2. seed
460	3. history
461	4. docs
462	5. semantic
463	6. facts, when present
464	
465	The pattern layer should be deterministic and token-free by default. Agent-assisted card synthesis can be optional later, but the initial path should produce usable cards from structured evidence.
466	
467	Status and overview integration:
468	
469	- `status` reports pattern source presence, freshness, counts, and update recommendations.
470	- `overview` includes the strongest current patterns.
471	- `brief` includes relevant patterns for the task.
472	- MCP exposes the same job-oriented surface: list patterns, status, and form only if the client explicitly asks for a write-capable action.
473	
474	## Implementation Phases
475	
476	### Phase 1: Episodes
477	
478	- Add `patterns` source manifest.
479	- Add episode extraction from exported sessions.
480	- Persist `patterns/episodes.ndjson`.
481	- Classify basic reinforcement.
482	- Add `entire brain patterns refresh`.
483	- Add `entire brain patterns status`.
484	- Test Codex and Claude transcript fixtures.
485	
486	### Phase 2: Procedures
487	
488	- Extract command and tool-sequence procedures.
489	- Build procedure ids and supporting synapses.
490	- Score repo-local procedure patterns.
491	- Add `entire brain patterns` read-only listing.
492	- Render basic pattern cards.
493	
494	### Phase 3: Practices
495	
496	- Use durable facts, history records, validation records, corrections, and read-only episodes to detect repeated practices.
497	- Score practices separately from procedures.
498	- Render practice cards with facts/history/source anchors.
499	
500	### Phase 4: Skill Memory
501	
502	- Add `patterns/skill-memory.ndjson`.
503	- Detect active, declined, changed, edited, and missing states.
504	- Add recommendations to `patterns status` and `patterns`.
505	- Test duplicate suppression and changed-evidence detection.
506	
507	### Phase 5: Skill Formation
508	
509	- Add `entire brain patterns form <pattern-id>`.
510	- Render full card and proposed skill draft before any write.
511	- Ask for an install destination, then write selected skill files only after confirmation.
512	- Store skill memory records.
513	- Refuse accidental overwrite without explicit confirmation.
514	
515	### Phase 6: Workspace Patterns
516	
517	- Add workspace pattern refresh/list/status/form commands.
518	- Aggregate member repo episodes and patterns.
519	- Preserve repo-specific variants.
520	- Score cross-repo and multi-author strength.
521	- Render workspace cards with repo breakdowns.
522	
523	### Phase 7: Agent/MCP Integration
524	
525	- Include relevant patterns in `brief`.
526	- Include strongest patterns in `overview`.
527	- Add MCP tools matching the public jobs.
528	- Add JSON contracts for patterns, cards, status, and form results.
529	
530	## Tests
531	
532	Add coverage for:
533	
534	- episode extraction from retained sessions
535	- actual command detection versus prose examples
536	- reinforcement classification
537	- procedure grouping
538	- practice grouping from facts and history
539	- synapse generation
540	- repo-local pattern scoring
541	- workspace pattern aggregation
542	- card rendering
543	- skill memory recommendations
544	- user-edited skill update detection
545	- skill formation without accidental overwrite
546	
547	## Suggested First PR
548	
549	Keep the first PR narrow:
550	
551	1. Add the `patterns` manifest source and storage paths.
552	2. Extract and persist `episodes.ndjson`.
553	3. Add `patterns refresh` and `patterns status`.
554	4. Add tests for episode extraction and reinforcement labels.
555	
556	Then add procedure grouping, cards, skill memory, and workspace consolidation in separate PRs.

## Vocabulary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Episode | One user request, the agent work that followed, and the next user feedback signal. |

| Practice | A repeated judgment, review, diagnosis, or model-steering behavior. |
| Pattern | A recurring procedure or practice. |
| Reinforcement | User approval, correction, commit/checkpoint success, or other feedback. |
| Consolidation | The process of turning a recurring pattern into a durable skill candidate. |
| Pattern card | Evidence summary shown to the user before skill creation or update. |

## Non-Goals

- Do not add developer-only CLI commands for raw episodes or synapses.
- Do not make the feature dependent on hosted model calls for the deterministic refresh path.
- Do not overwrite user-edited skill files without explicit confirmation.
- Do not replace durable facts, semantic graph inspection, or retrieval. Patterns are a new layer built from those sources.

## Storage Model

Add a `patterns` source to the brain manifest:

```json
{
  "sources": {
    "patterns": {
      "generated_at": "2026-06-16T00:00:00Z",
      "episodes": 1234,
      "procedures": 42,
      "practices": 18,
      "patterns": 12,
      "skill_memory": 5,
      "fingerprint": "sha256:..."
    }
  }
}
```

Persist derived data under the brain directory:

```text
patterns/
  episodes.ndjson
  procedures.ndjson
  practices.ndjson
  patterns.ndjson
  synapses.ndjson
  cards/
    <pattern-id>.json
    <pattern-id>.md
  skill-memory.ndjson
```

Use the existing brain write lock and atomic write helpers. Treat all files as derived and rebuildable except `skill-memory.ndjson`, which is user-state and must be preserved across refreshes.

## Episode Layer

Build episodes from exported session transcripts. An episode is the normalized unit used by pattern detection:

```json
{
  "id": "episode:...",
  "repo_key": "gh/ashtom/entire-brain",
  "workspace": "platform",
  "session_id": "...",
  "checkpoint_id": "...",
  "branch": "main",
  "author": "Thomas Dohmke",
  "agent": "Codex",
  "intent": "review release readiness",
  "intent_signature": "review:release",
  "tool_sequence": ["search", "read", "edit", "test"],
  "command_sequence": ["go test ./...", "gofmt -w ."],
  "files": ["internal/cli/refresh.go"],
  "reinforcement": "success",
  "source": {
    "path": "sessions/main/...",
    "line": 123
  }
}
```

Episode extraction should:

- Count only actual agent tool calls and executed commands, not examples in prose.
- Preserve source anchors into retained transcripts.
- Classify reinforcement from the next user turn and available Entire checkpoint/session metadata.
- Keep branch, repo, author, agent, and workspace identity on every episode.
- Be deterministic and safe to run during `refresh`.

## Synapse Graph

Use synapses internally to preserve why a pattern exists:

```json
{
  "from": "episode:abc",
  "to": "procedure:def",
  "kind": "supports",
  "weight": 0.82,
  "evidence": "sessions/main/...:123"
}
```

Initial synapse kinds:

- `supports`: an episode supports a procedure, practice, fact, symbol, or pattern.
- `reinforces`: a reinforcement signal strengthens or weakens a procedure/practice.
- `mentions`: an episode refers to a file, symbol, command, or fact.
- `varies`: a repo-specific procedure variant belongs to a workspace-level pattern.
- `contradicts`: a correction or later fact weakens a prior pattern interpretation.

Do not expose synapses as commands. They are internal evidence edges used for scoring, cards, and future debugging through files/tests.

## Pattern Detection

Detect two pattern families.

### Procedures

Procedures come from repeated operational shapes:

- command n-grams within an episode
- tool-sequence shapes
- repeated file/path clusters
- validation loops
- branch, release, review, or benchmark workflows

### Practices

Practices come from repeated judgment and interaction:

- durable facts with kinds such as `preference`, `convention`, `gotcha`, `decision`, and `closed-negative`
- history records around validations, corrections, and reviews
- conversational or read-only episodes
- repeated user steering or verification expectations

Each pattern receives a stable id, type, scope, strength, source anchors, supporting episodes, and variant metadata.

Strength should include:

```text
recurrence
+ span over time
+ recency
+ specificity
+ reinforcement quality
+ repo count
+ author count
+ branch count
```

## Workspace Semantics

Workspace support is a core design requirement.

There are two scopes:

| Scope | Meaning | Skill implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo | Repeats inside one repository. | Good for repo-local or repo-specific skills. |
| Workspace | Repeats across multiple repos in a workspace. | Strong signal for portable or team skills. |

Pattern identity must include scope:

```json
{
  "id": "pattern:...",
  "scope": "repo",
  "repo_key": "gh/entireio/cli",
  "workspace": ""
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "pattern:...",
  "scope": "workspace",
  "repo_key": "",
  "workspace": "platform"
}
```

Workspace consolidation should:

- Load member repo brains by workspace membership.
- Combine repo-local episodes without copying generated brain data between repos.
- Notice procedures and practices that recur across repos.
- Preserve repo-specific variants.
- Reward patterns that recur across repos and authors.
- Render pattern cards with a repo breakdown.

Example card section:

```text
Seen in:
- api: 5 episodes, 3 success, 1 corrected
- web: 4 episodes, 2 success
- cli: 7 episodes, 5 success

Common procedure:
...

Repo-specific variations:
- api uses ...
- web uses ...
```

## Public Commands

Keep the public command surface aligned to user jobs.

### Repo Commands

```sh
entire brain patterns
entire brain patterns refresh
entire brain patterns status
entire brain patterns form <pattern-id>
```

`entire brain patterns`

Default read-only view. Shows strongest current patterns with concise evidence summaries and ids.

Options:

```sh
--json
--limit N
--type procedure|practice
--scope repo|workspace
```

`entire brain patterns refresh`

Rebuilds the pattern layer from current brain sources. `entire brain refresh` should run this by default after sessions, history, facts, docs, and semantic sources are current.

Options:

```sh
--force
--json
```

`entire brain patterns status`

Shows freshness and skill memory state:

```text
patterns: current
episodes: 1234
procedures: 42
practices: 18
accepted skills: 5
declined patterns: 3
updates available: 2
```

Options:

```sh
--json
```

`entire brain patterns form <pattern-id>`

Shows the full pattern card, prepares a proposed `SKILL.md` draft, then asks where, if anywhere, to install it. The command must not write files until the user chooses a destination.

Options:

```sh
--name <skill-name>
--destination global|repo
--yes
--json
```

In non-interactive mode, require both `--name` and `--yes`.

### Workspace Commands

Mirror the repo commands without expanding the surface:

```sh
entire brain workspace patterns <workspace>
entire brain workspace patterns refresh <workspace>
entire brain workspace patterns status <workspace>
entire brain workspace patterns form <workspace> <pattern-id>
```

Workspace `patterns` should show cross-repo patterns by default and include repo breakdowns in each card.

## Pattern Cards

A pattern card is the approval surface for skill creation or update.

Card shape:

```text
Pattern: release-readiness-evidence
Type: procedure
Scope: workspace
Strength: high
Reinforcement: 12 success, 2 corrected, 9 neutral
Seen in: 8 sessions, 3 repos, 2 authors

What repeats:
...

Trigger:
Use when ...

Evidence:
- session/checkpoint/path:line
- real command/tool sequence
- supporting fact ids

Would become:
- Steps
- Verification
- Failure modes
```

Rules:

- Always show a card before asking the user to form or update a skill.
- Include retained source anchors.
- Include corrections and failure modes when available.
- Distinguish common workflow from repo-specific variants.
- Do not include raw transcripts or secrets.

## Skill Memory

Track user decisions in `patterns/skill-memory.ndjson`:

```json
{
  "pattern_id": "pattern:...",
  "scope": "repo",
  "status": "active",
  "skill_name": "verify-release-readiness",
  "skill_path": "~/.agents/skills/verify-release-readiness/SKILL.md",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "content_sha": "sha256:...",
  "sessions": 8,
  "reinforcement": {
    "success": 12,
    "corrected": 2,
    "neutral": 9
  },
  "created_at": "2026-06-16T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-06-16T00:00:00Z",
  "note": ""
}
```

Recommendations:

- `active/current`: accepted skill exists and evidence has not materially changed.
- `active/update`: evidence changed materially; offer update.
- `active/edited`: skill file changed since formation; present a careful update plan.
- `declined/current`: suppress.
- `declined/reconsider`: evidence materially changed; show what changed before asking again.
- `missing`: skill memory points to a missing file; offer to recreate or forget.

## Skill Formation

`patterns form` prepares a skill draft from the selected pattern card. It writes selected skills only after the user chooses an install destination.

Interactive flow:

1. Render the full pattern card.
2. Render the proposed `SKILL.md` draft.
3. Ask where to install it:
   - Global: `~/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`
   - Repo-local: if a repo-local convention is implemented
   - Draft only: print the draft without writing
   - Cancel
4. Write only after the user chooses a write destination.

The initial implementation may support only global install, draft-only output, and cancel. Add repo-local or workspace-local destinations after the project settles those conventions.

Default destination:

```text
~/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
```

Repo-local destination:

```text
<repo>/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
```

If the project settles on a different repo-local convention, use that consistently and document it in `README.md`.

Generated skill shape:

```markdown
---
name: <name>
description: Use when ...
---

# <Name>

## Steps

...

## Verification

...

## Failure Modes

...

## Evidence

Formed by Entire Brain from N sessions with retained source anchors.
```

Skill body rules:

- Keep steps focused on future behavior, not session recap.
- Include verification when evidence shows how work was checked.
- Include failure modes from corrections.
- Keep source anchors concise.
- Never write or overwrite a file before the destination choice is explicit.
- Recompute and store `content_sha` after writing.

## Refresh Integration

`entire brain refresh` should run pattern refresh after:

1. sessions
2. seed
3. history
4. docs
5. semantic
6. facts, when present

The pattern layer should be deterministic and token-free by default. Agent-assisted card synthesis can be optional later, but the initial path should produce usable cards from structured evidence.

Status and overview integration:

- `status` reports pattern source presence, freshness, counts, and update recommendations.
- `overview` includes the strongest current patterns.
- `brief` includes relevant patterns for the task.
- MCP exposes the same job-oriented surface: list patterns, status, and form only if the client explicitly asks for a write-capable action.

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Episodes

- Add `patterns` source manifest.
- Add episode extraction from exported sessions.
- Persist `patterns/episodes.ndjson`.
- Classify basic reinforcement.
- Add `entire brain patterns refresh`.
- Add `entire brain patterns status`.
- Test Codex and Claude transcript fixtures.

### Phase 2: Procedures

- Extract command and tool-sequence procedures.
- Build procedure ids and supporting synapses.
- Score repo-local procedure patterns.
- Add `entire brain patterns` read-only listing.
- Render basic pattern cards.

### Phase 3: Practices

- Use durable facts, history records, validation records, corrections, and read-only episodes to detect repeated practices.
- Score practices separately from procedures.
- Render practice cards with facts/history/source anchors.

### Phase 4: Skill Memory

- Add `patterns/skill-memory.ndjson`.
- Detect active, declined, changed, edited, and missing states.
- Add recommendations to `patterns status` and `patterns`.
- Test duplicate suppression and changed-evidence detection.

### Phase 5: Skill Formation

- Add `entire brain patterns form <pattern-id>`.
- Render full card and proposed skill draft before any write.
- Ask for an install destination, then write selected skill files only after confirmation.
- Store skill memory records.
- Refuse accidental overwrite without explicit confirmation.

### Phase 6: Workspace Patterns

- Add workspace pattern refresh/list/status/form commands.
- Aggregate member repo episodes and patterns.
- Preserve repo-specific variants.
- Score cross-repo and multi-author strength.
- Render workspace cards with repo breakdowns.

### Phase 7: Agent/MCP Integration

- Include relevant patterns in `brief`.
- Include strongest patterns in `overview`.
- Add MCP tools matching the public jobs.
- Add JSON contracts for patterns, cards, status, and form results.

## Tests

Add coverage for:

- episode extraction from retained sessions
- actual command detection versus prose examples
- reinforcement classification
- procedure grouping
- practice grouping from facts and history
- synapse generation
- repo-local pattern scoring
- workspace pattern aggregation
- card rendering
- skill memory recommendations
- user-edited skill update detection
- skill formation without accidental overwrite

## Suggested First PR

Keep the first PR narrow:

1. Add the `patterns` manifest source and storage paths.
2. Extract and persist `episodes.ndjson`.
3. Add `patterns refresh` and `patterns status`.
4. Add tests for episode extraction and reinforcement labels.

Then add procedure grouping, cards, skill memory, and workspace consolidation in separate PRs.

Now I have enough information. Let me compile the comprehensive findings.

## Summary of Findings

Based on my analysis of the entire-brain codebase, here are the details on the four subsystems you're reviewing:

### 1. DURABLE FACTS: Structure and Kinds

**File:** `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts.go` (lines 85-114) and `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go` (lines 47-59)

**Fact Record Structure** (`factRecord`):
- `ID` (string): content-derived sha256 hash (normalized text + sorted paths)
- `Paths` ([]string): 1-2 taxonomy paths (topic labels, validated against `factPathPattern`)
- `Kind` (string): closed classification
- `Locus` ([]string): code identifiers/paths the fact is about
- `Text` (string): third-person statement about the user
- `Branch` (string): git branch
- `Origin` (string): "distilled" or "authored"
- `Status` (string): "active", "superseded", or "retracted"
- `Confidence` (string): optional confidence label
- `Provenance` ([]factAnchor): >=1 source anchors with SessionID, CheckpointID, TurnID, Transcript path, Line
- `RelatedIDs` ([]string): linked fact IDs
- `SupersededBy` (string): ID of superseding fact
- `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt` (time.Time)

**FACT KINDS - Actual Set (NOT what the plan says):**

The code defines **SIX** kinds, not five as your plan notes:

1. `factKindDecision = "decision"` — a resolved choice + its rationale
2. `factKindInvariant = "invariant"` — a must-hold rule/constraint
3. `factKindGotcha = "gotcha"` — a non-obvious trap/footgun
4. `factKindPreference = "preference"` — how the user likes work done
5. `factKindConvention = "convention"` — a standing process/style norm
6. `factKindClosedNegative = "closed-negative"` — what was tried/considered and rejected with evidence, why it failed, when to revisit

**MISMATCH ALERT:** Your plan lists `closed-negative` but this is implemented as `closed-negative` (hyphenated), not as a separate item from the five you named.

**Extraction: NON-Deterministic (LLM-based)**

Facts are extracted by an LLM agent during distillation:
- `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/distill_cmd.go` shows facts are extracted via agent calls (claude-code, codex, ollama, or command)
- The agent emits JSON lines with fact text, paths, and optionally a kind
- **Inference path exists for deterministic backfill** (`inferFactKind` in `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go` lines 119-155): when an agent-emitted kind is missing or invalid, a deterministic classifier uses:
  - **High-precision phrase cues** checked in order: `closedNegativeCues` → `gotchaCues` → `invariantCues`
  - **Taxonomy prior:** top-level category maps to default kind (e.g., constraints → invariant, preferences → preference)
  - **Priority tiebreak:** when multi-path, higher-priority kind wins (closedNegative=6, gotcha=5, invariant=4, preference=3, convention=2, decision=1)

**Kind Schema Definition Location:**
- Constants: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go:47-59`
- Validation: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go:63-75`
- Inference logic: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go:119-155`

---

### 2. HISTORY RECORDS: Structure and Types

**File:** `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go` (lines 51-78)

**History Record Structure** (`historyRecord`):
- `ID` (string): derived from (file path, line number, kind, normalized text)
- `Kind` (string): extracted record type
- `Branch` (string, optional): git branch the transcript belongs to
- `Path` (string): brain-relative transcript file path
- `Line` (int): line number in the transcript
- `Summary` (string): truncated (~700 chars) cleaned transcript text
- `Terms` ([]string, optional): indexed search terms extracted from Summary

**HISTORY RECORD KINDS - What Actually Exists:**

The code extracts **SEVEN** kinds from transcripts via `classifyHistoryFragment` (lines 873-908):

1. `"request"` — user prompts (wrapper-filtered, Phase 4 re-introduced for handoff/midtask eval)
2. `"decision"` — agent statements about choices and rationale
3. `"learning"` — agent insights (root cause, lessons learned)
4. `"validation"` — testing and verification statements
5. `"architecture"` — system design statements
6. `"tool_call"` — tool invocations (exec_command, apply_patch, read, write, git grep, etc.)
7. `"code_fact"` — code snippets extracted from tool results containing signal keywords

**MISMATCH ALERT:** Your plan mentions "validations, corrections, and reviews" as distinct history record types. **This does NOT exist.** What exists:
- `"validation"` records are extracted from lines mentioning test-related keywords (see line 893)
- **NO separate `"correction"` or `"review"` record kinds exist in the current code**
- Records anchor to lines in transcripts; there is no separate "correction metadata" structure

**Extraction:** Extraction is **deterministic, heuristic-based** (NO LLM calls):
- Scans transcript JSON/JSONL/markdown line-by-line
- Applies cheap keyword fast-path filter (`historyLineMayContainIndexedContent`)
- Extracts JSON fragments for kind-specific content
- Classifies via phrase matching (no agent inference)
- IDs are stable sha256(path + line + kind + text)
- Results cached by (file size, mtime) to skip re-parsing (`historyScanCache`)

**History Index and Source Manifest:**
- Index file: `/internal/cli/history.go:64-68` (`historyIndex`)
- Source manifest: `/internal/cli/history.go:51-62` (`historySourceManifest`) with counters: Decisions, Learnings, Validations, ToolCalls, CodeFacts

---

### 3. REINFORCEMENT SIGNALS: Current State (Minimal)

**FINDING: No explicit reinforcement/feedback signal classification exists yet.**

What the code DOES track:
- **Checkpoint metadata** (`checkpointExportSession` in `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/export.go`): SessionID, Agent, Model, Kind, Error, TokenUsage, Summary — but NO success/failure classification
- **Validation records** (`"validation"` kind in history) are extracted from test-related phrases, but there is no mechanism to link them to user feedback or checkpoint outcomes
- **Fact provenance** includes CheckpointID anchors, but checkpoint success/failure is not recorded on the fact itself

**What DOES NOT exist:**
- No classification of reinforcement as "success", "corrected", or "neutral"
- No structure linking user corrections to facts
- No feedback signal attached to checkpoint metadata
- No "next user turn" analysis to classify outcomes

**Closest analogues:**
- Facts have `Status` (active/superseded/retracted) but this is a static lifecycle marker, not a reinforcement signal
- History validation records exist but are not connected to agent performance feedback
- Checkpoint metadata exists but lacks success/failure outcome fields

---

### 4. EMBEDDINGS & SEMANTIC GRAPH: Current State

**File:** `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/embed.go` (lines 15-49) and `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/embedmodel.go`

**Embedder Interface** (lines 25-31):
```go
type Embedder interface {
	Embed(text string) []float32
	Dim() int
	ID() string // model+revision fingerprint for cache invalidation
}
```

**Current Implementation:**
- **Static Embedder:** `staticEmbedder` (lines 33-49) — pure-Go Model2Vec implementation
- **Binary format:** int8 per-column quantized matrix with BERT WordPiece tokenization
- **Bundled:** `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/embedmodel.go` — embedded as asset `assets/embedmodel.bin`
- **Tokenization:** BERT BertNormalizer + BertPreTokenizer + WordPiece (deterministic, no model calls)
- **Inference:** mean-pool of dequantized token vectors → L2-normalize
- **Offline:** no network, no cgo dependency, single static binary

**Semantic Graph / Symbols:**
- **Semantic records** defined in `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/semantic.go` (lines 133-154)
- Record types: `"symbol"`, `"relation"` (from `record_type` field)
- Symbol fields: ID, Kind, Name, QualifiedName, FilePath, StartLine, EndLine, Signature, Language
- Relation fields: FromID, ToID, Type (e.g., "HANDLES_WORKFLOW"), Confidence

**Usage:**
- History vectors: opt-in via `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER` environment variable (see lines 154-178)
- Fact embedding: available but vector store persistence is gated
- Semantic indexing: separate `semantic index` command with snapshot/store/generation

**MISMATCH ALERT:** Your reference to "Phase D embeddings: pure-Go static embeddings behind an Embedder interface" is **accurate** — this is already implemented. The **semantic graph source is separate** — symbols/relations are extracted by an external semantic provider and stored in snapshot/store, not built from the Embedder interface.

---

## Summary of Mismatches with Design Plan

| Plan Item | Reality | Issue |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| Fact kinds: `preference`, `convention`, `gotcha`, `decision`, `closed-negative` | Implemented correctly, but code shows **6 kinds** not 5 | The plan may have missed that there are 6, or conflated kinds |

| Semantic graph source and symbols | Symbols/relations exist but sourced from **external semantic provider**, not built from embeddings | Embedder is for ranking/retrieval, not semantic graph source |

---

   - Schema: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts.go:85-114`
   - Kinds: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go:47-75`

- `ID` (string): content-derived sha256 hash (normalized text + sorted paths)
- `Paths` ([]string): 1-2 taxonomy paths (topic labels, validated against `factPathPattern`)
- `Kind` (string): closed classification
- `Locus` ([]string): code identifiers/paths the fact is about
- `Text` (string): third-person statement about the user
- `Branch` (string): git branch
- `Origin` (string): "distilled" or "authored"
- `Status` (string): "active", "superseded", or "retracted"
- `Confidence` (string): optional confidence label
- `Provenance` ([]factAnchor): >=1 source anchors with SessionID, CheckpointID, TurnID, Transcript path, Line
- `RelatedIDs` ([]string): linked fact IDs
- `SupersededBy` (string): ID of superseding fact
- `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt` (time.Time)

**FACT KINDS - Actual Set (NOT what the plan says):**

The code defines **SIX** kinds, not five as your plan notes:

1. `factKindDecision = "decision"` — a resolved choice + its rationale
2. `factKindInvariant = "invariant"` — a must-hold rule/constraint
3. `factKindGotcha = "gotcha"` — a non-obvious trap/footgun
4. `factKindPreference = "preference"` — how the user likes work done
5. `factKindConvention = "convention"` — a standing process/style norm
6. `factKindClosedNegative = "closed-negative"` — what was tried/considered and rejected with evidence, why it failed, when to revisit

**MISMATCH ALERT:** Your plan lists `closed-negative` but this is implemented as `closed-negative` (hyphenated), not as a separate item from the five you named.

**Extraction: NON-Deterministic (LLM-based)**

Facts are extracted by an LLM agent during distillation:
- `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/distill_cmd.go` shows facts are extracted via agent calls (claude-code, codex, ollama, or command)
- The agent emits JSON lines with fact text, paths, and optionally a kind
- **Inference path exists for deterministic backfill** (`inferFactKind` in `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go` lines 119-155): when an agent-emitted kind is missing or invalid, a deterministic classifier uses:
  - **High-precision phrase cues** checked in order: `closedNegativeCues` → `gotchaCues` → `invariantCues`
  - **Taxonomy prior:** top-level category maps to default kind (e.g., constraints → invariant, preferences → preference)
  - **Priority tiebreak:** when multi-path, higher-priority kind wins (closedNegative=6, gotcha=5, invariant=4, preference=3, convention=2, decision=1)

**Kind Schema Definition Location:**
- Constants: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go:47-59`
- Validation: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/facts_locus.go:63-75`

### 2. HISTORY RECORDS: Structure and Types

**File:** `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go` (lines 51-78)

- `ID` (string): derived from (file path, line number, kind, normalized text)

- `Branch` (string, optional): git branch the transcript belongs to
- `Path` (string): brain-relative transcript file path
- `Line` (int): line number in the transcript

4. `"validation"` — testing and verification statements
5. `"architecture"` — system design statements

- Scans transcript JSON/JSONL/markdown line-by-line
- Applies cheap keyword fast-path filter (`historyLineMayContainIndexedContent`)
- Extracts JSON fragments for kind-specific content
- Classifies via phrase matching (no agent inference)
- IDs are stable sha256(path + line + kind + text)
- Results cached by (file size, mtime) to skip re-parsing (`historyScanCache`)

## Key Findings for Design Doc Assessment

1. **No built-in "patterns" source yet** — all sources are pre-defined in brainSources struct. Adding "patterns" would require:

   - Atomic write via writeBrainRelativeFileAtomic

   - Idempotent on re-distill (upsert by ID)
   - Durable as NDJSON with provenance anchors

3. **Write locks are global per brain** — all sources compete for the single write.lock. The refresh pipeline runs unlocked between stages (line 287 comment in export.go: "transcript-writing phase between them runs UNLOCKED"). This is intentional for parallelism; ensure patterns follows the same pattern.

4. **No "fingerprint" concept in manifest** — freshness is tracked per-source (SessionsFingerprint for history, WorktreeHash for semantic). Your patterns design should define its own staleness signal.

5. **Workspace is optional** — single-repo brains work fine; workspace is an overlay for multi-repo coordination. Patterns should work both standalone and in workspace mode.

6. **MCP is request/response, no persistent jobs** — each tool call is stateless. If patterns need background synthesis, that's a separate async surface (like seed agent synthesis).

I've read the plan and cross-checked its assumptions against the actual `entire-brain` code. Here's my review.

## Verdict

This is a strong, well-structured design — the vocabulary discipline, evidence-first pattern cards, the skill-memory state machine, and treating workspace scope as first-class are all the right calls, and they fit the existing brain architecture (manifest sources, per-branch ndjson, global write lock, atomic writes, workspace membership resolution all exist and match what the plan assumes).

But the plan rests on **three load-bearing assumptions about existing data that aren't true in the code today**, and the riskiest piece of new work is buried inside Phase 1 as if it were minor. Below, grounded in the source.

## Load-bearing gaps (fix before Phase 1)

**1. Reinforcement classification doesn't exist — and the whole design depends on it.**
There is no code today that classifies a turn/checkpoint as `success` / `corrected` / `neutral`. Checkpoint metadata (`checkpointExportSession` in `export.go`) carries `Error`, `TokenUsage`, `Summary` — but no outcome label. Facts have a `Status` lifecycle (active/superseded/retracted), not a feedback signal. Yet reinforcement feeds the strength formula, the card header ("12 success, 2 corrected"), and the skill-memory `reinforcement` block. The plan lists "classify basic reinforcement" as one bullet in Phase 1 next to plumbing — it's actually the hardest and most novel component. **Recommend: pull it out as an explicit spike with a written rubric** (what textual/metadata signals map to each label, and the precision you'll accept) before committing to the card format that advertises these counts.

**2. "history records around validations, corrections, and reviews" — only `validation` exists.**
`classifyHistoryFragment` (history.go:873-908) produces: `request`, `decision`, `learning`, `validation`, `architecture`, `tool_call`, `code_fact`. There is **no `correction` and no `review` record kind.** This matters because the Practices detector (Phase 3) and the card "Failure modes from corrections" both assume correction signal is sittable. It isn't — you'd derive corrections from the same unbuilt reinforcement classifier. So failure-mode sections will be empty or hand-wavy unless that classifier lands first.

**3. The "Episode" unit doesn't exist and crosses a boundary the data doesn't cleanly provide.**
The unit is "request + agent work + *next user feedback signal*." Sessions/checkpoints exist; turn structure exists in the v2 `transcript.jsonl`; history has a `request` kind. But "the next user turn" as a linkable, classifiable signal isn't modeled anywhere. Specify exactly how an episode is bounded (within a checkpoint? across checkpoints in a session?) and where the "next feedback" turn comes from — otherwise episode extraction in Phase 1 is underspecified.

## Substantive design issues

**4. Pattern-id stability is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have.** `skill-memory.ndjson` is keyed on `pattern_id` and is the one file you preserve across refreshes. If pattern ids drift between refreshes (e.g., recomputed from a changing episode set), every skill-memory linkage breaks silently. The plan says "stable id" but doesn't define derivation. Facts and history already solve this — content-hash ids (`sha256(normalized content + sorted anchors)`). **Specify the same scheme for patterns and state the invariant explicitly:** a pattern's identity must not change when unrelated episodes are added.

**5. Strength is an unweighted wish-list.** The formula is eight `+` terms with no weights, no normalization, and no thresholds mapping to high/medium/low. Without that, "strongest patterns" and the card `Strength: high` are undefined, and you'll get noise: ubiquitous procedures like `go test ./...` / `gofmt -w .` will dominate every repo. The `specificity` term gestures at this but needs teeth — an idf-style down-weighting of universal commands. (Your memory note on the two divergent query-tokenizer/stopword regimes is directly relevant here; reuse that machinery rather than inventing a third.) **Recommend: concrete weights + a documented high/med/low cutoff in Phase 2.**

**6. Do you need `synapses.ndjson` in v1?** The plan itself says synapses are internal-only and partly for "future debugging." A whole edge-store persistence layer is real cost, and patterns already carry `supporting episodes` + `source anchors`. I'd **defer the persisted synapse graph** and keep evidence as anchors on the pattern record until something actually consumes edges. Less to build, less to keep consistent across refresh.

**7. Manifest `fingerprint` doesn't match how the codebase tracks freshness.** There's no central per-source `fingerprint` field; freshness is per-source and signal-specific (`SessionsFingerprint` for history, `WorktreeHash` for semantic). Define the patterns staleness signal as a function of its *inputs* (sessions fingerprint + facts presence + history index), so `patterns status: current/stale` is computable the same way the other sources do it.

**8. Facts are LLM-distilled and often absent — practices must degrade gracefully.** Fact distillation isn't in the deterministic `refresh` pipeline (refresh.go order is sessions → seed → history → history-vectors → docs → semantic → branch overlays); facts come from a separate agent-based `distill`. The plan correctly says "facts, when present," but Phase 3 Practices leans heavily on facts. State explicitly that practices yield an empty (not broken) result when no facts exist, so the deterministic/token-free guarantee holds. Also: fact kinds are **six**, not the five listed — you omit `invariant`, which is a strong practice signal (must-hold rules). Add it.

## Smaller notes

- **Incrementality:** episodes.ndjson over all history could be large and refresh runs often. Reuse the existing `historyScanCache` (size+mtime keyed) pattern so refresh is incremental, not full-rescan. Worth a sentence in the Refresh section.
- **Secret hygiene:** "Do not include raw transcripts or secrets" is the right rule, but cards show "real command/tool sequence" and commands routinely contain tokens (URLs, env). Add a redaction pass, and prefer `path:line` anchors over inlined command text where possible.
- **Skill install path:** verify `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is the path the harness actually reads before standardizing on it — confirm against the real skills lookup, since getting this wrong means formed skills are invisible.
- **Phase 1 ships empty:** `patterns`/`status` with only episodes will report 0 procedures/practices. Fine as scaffolding, but say so, so it doesn't read as a regression.
- **Write-lock discipline:** patterns refresh must go through `withBrainWriteLock`; note that the existing pipeline deliberately runs transcript-writing *unlocked* between locked stages — follow that same shape rather than holding the lock across the whole pattern build.

## Suggested phase reordering

Move reinforcement from "a bullet in Phase 1" to a **Phase 0 spike** (rubric + precision target), because Phases 2, 3, and the card format all encode its output. Everything else can stay. The "narrow first PR" (manifest source + episodes.ndjson + refresh/status + tests) is correctly scoped — just add the reinforcement rubric to it, or explicitly defer reinforcement out of episodes until the spike lands.

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me compile the findings into a concise report for the user.

## Distill End-to-End Analysis

### 1. Command Surface: `entire brain distill`

**Registration**: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/root.go:89`

**Command**: `distill [path]` (default searches for a brain at the repo root)

**Subcommands**: None (distill is a leaf command)

**Flags**:
- `--branch`: Limit to a single branch (default: all)
- `--session`: Limit to a single session ID (incompatible with `--force`)
- `--force`: Recompute all facts from scratch (drops distilled facts, keeps authored)
- `--json`: Emit the fact source summary as JSON
- `--agent`: `auto` (resolved to codex/claude-code), `codex`, `claude-code`, `ollama`, or `command`
- `--agent-command`: Custom agent argv for `--agent command`
- `--model`: Override the agent model (e.g., specific GPT version)
- `--effort`: Override reasoning effort (e.g., `low`)
- `--dry-run`: Estimate work without calling an agent
- `--concurrency`: Pool size for in-flight agent calls (default 4, ≥1 = sequential)
- `--jobs`: Alias for `--concurrency`
- `--max-chunk-bytes`: Transcript chunk size (default 48KB; long-context models handle 128–192KB)
- `--confidence`: Confidence threshold for auto-applying merge/supersede (default 0.75)

Defined in: `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:473–504` (`newDistillCommand`)

---

### 2. Pipeline End-to-End

**Input**:
- Reads exported sessions from the brain manifest (`manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions`)
- Sessions are in chronological order (sorted by `CreatedAt`)
- For each session, reads its transcript file (JSONL or document-form JSON)

**Processing stages**:

1. **Preprocessing** (lines 1251–1316): Strips tool calls, tool outputs, session/meta records, leaving only human/assistant conversation text. Document-form transcripts (JSON documents with `messages` field) are parsed separately. Blank lines are preserved for line numbering but not emitted.

2. **Fingerprinting & Cache Check** (lines 1573–1599): Computes a SHA256 fingerprint of `(SessionID, LatestCheckpoint, resolved_branch, cacheSalt, sha256(preprocessed_text))`. If unchanged and not `--force`, the session is cached and skipped (no agent calls).

3. **Chunking** (lines 1507–1571): Splits the preprocessed text into chunks no larger than `--max-chunk-bytes` (default 48KB), preserving 1-based line numbers. Chunks are annotated with `StartLine` and `EndLine` so provenance anchors point to exact line ranges.

4. **Agent Extraction** (lines 879–911): For each chunk not cached, invokes the agent with:
   - System prompt: rendered distill template (with taxonomy block substituted)
   - Stdin: line-numbered chunk text
   - Output: parsed line-by-line for facts
   - **Parallelism**: controlled by `--concurrency` semaphore; at concurrency=1, calls are serialized and lazy (only made for chunks the consumer actually consumes).

5. **Fact Parsing** (lines 178–257 in `distill.go`): Each agent output line parsed as `[kind<TAB>]path[,path]<TAB>fact`:
   - Kind (optional): one of {decision, invariant, gotcha, preference, convention, closed-negative}; inferred if absent/invalid
   - Paths: normalized (lowercase, deduplicated, capped at 2), filtered by taxonomy (only known top-level categories kept)
   - Text: truncated to 2000 chars; lowercased, whitespace-collapsed for ID computation
   - Output capped at 6 facts per chunk

6. **Reconciliation** (lines 303–332 in `reconcile.go`): For each chunk's candidates, compares against existing active facts at the same paths:
   - No matches → all candidates treated as `new`
   - Matches → invokes reconcile agent with both lists (candidates + top-50 recent existing facts)
   - Agent output: `<candidate#> <decision> <existing#-or-dash> <confidence>`
   - Decisions: `new` (1.0 confidence), `merge` (consolidate into existing), `supersede` (replace)
   - **Confidence gate**: if confidence ≥ threshold (0.75), action auto-applies; else queued as proposal for manual review

7. **Merge/Supersede** (lines 46–108 in `facts_merge.go`):
   - `new`: upsert (idempotent by ID)
   - `merge` (high conf): union provenance, drop candidate
   - `supersede` (high conf): mark target as `superseded`, add candidate as active replacement
   - Low-conf actions: both facts stay active, cross-linked via `RelatedIDs`, queued for review

8. **Persistence**: In-memory facts flushed every ~50 agent calls (midrun checkpoints); final flush after all sessions. Cache saved (JSON) alongside facts. On resume, idempotent by ID.

**Incremental vs. Full**:
- **Default (incremental)**: Skips sessions with matching fingerprints (cache hits). On resume, flushed facts are re-visited but deduplicated (same ID).
- **`--force`**: Drops all distilled facts before starting; force rebuilds from scratch. Prompts read on final flush only (mid-run flushes drop prior proposal backlog).
- **`--session <id>`**: Fast single-session path; carries other sessions' cache entries through unchanged.

**Output**: Manifest record (`sources.facts`) with counts (facts, distilled, authored, superseded), agent calls, timing, warnings; proposals queued if any low-confidence actions.

---

### 3. Agent/Model Invocation

**Command builders** (`distill.go:105–176`):
- **codex**: `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules --sandbox read-only [--model M] [--config model_reasoning_effort=E] <prompt>`
- **claude-code**: `claude --print --no-session-persistence --setting-sources user --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --disable-slash-commands --permission-mode dontAsk --tools '' [--model M] [--effort E] --system-prompt <prompt>`
- **ollama**: `ollama [model] <prompt>` (HTTP POST to loopback-only endpoint, default `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate`)
- **command**: User-supplied argv (no injection)

**Prompt** (`distill.go:54–66`): Rendered from shipped template `/templates/entire-brain-distill.md` with taxonomy block substituted. Key sections:
- SILENT DEFAULT: output nothing for most turns; only emit when all four checks pass (durable, useful, not-known, worth-writing)
- ALWAYS-CAPTURE TRIGGERS: standing rules, stated preferences, resolved decisions, project facts, non-obvious knowledge, negatively-settled questions
- Output format: `kind<TAB>path[,path]<TAB>fact` (exactly 0–6 lines per chunk)

**Reconcile prompt** (`reconcile.go:100–131`): Static, lists candidates and existing facts, agent outputs `<candidate#> <decision> <existing#-or-dash> <confidence>` (one line per candidate, strict grammar).

**Output contract**:
- Distill: line-based, `kind<TAB>path<TAB>fact`; agent omissions/synonyms recovered; capped at 6/chunk
- Reconcile: line-based, `<num> <decision> <ref> <confidence>`; missing lines default to `new`; malformed lines downgrade to `new` with warning

---

### 4. Validation, Normalization, Kind Inference, Deduplication, Merging

**Validation & Normalization** (facts.go:156–175):
- Paths: lowercase, trim, drop syntactically invalid (must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z0-9_]+){2}$`), deduplicate, sort, cap at 2
- Text: whitespace collapsed, lowercased (for ID only; stored case-preserved)
- Kind: validated against closed set {decision, invariant, gotcha, preference, convention, closed-negative}; invalid/absent kinds inferred

**Kind inference** (facts_locus.go:119–156):
- Closed-negative cues ("dead end", "ruled out", "didn't work because", …) → `closed-negative` (highest priority)
- Gotcha cues ("gotcha", "footgun", "subtle bug", "surprising", …) → `gotcha`
- Invariant cues ("must", "never", "always", …) → `invariant`
- Top-level category prior: preferences→preference, workflow→convention, constraints→invariant, architecture/project→decision
- Fallback: decision

**Locus extraction** (facts_locus.go:245–268): Regex match for backtick spans and identifier patterns (dotted paths, CamelCase, snake_case); lowercased, 3+ chars, deduplicated, sorted.

**Deduplication & Merging**:

- **By ID** (`upsertFact`, facts.go:287–305): Content-derived ID = sha256(normalize(text) + "\x00" + join(sorted_paths, ",")). Same ID → union provenance anchors, advance UpdatedAt, fill Kind if absent/invalid.
- **Reconciliation deduplication** (distill.go:303–332): Agent decides merge (same meaning) vs. supersede (contradicts) vs. new. Merge unions anchors; supersede retains old fact (marked `superseded`), adds new as active.
- **Proposal deduplication** (reconcile.go:68–86): Dedupe by (action, candidate_id, target_id); stable-sorted by target_id, then candidate_id.

**Provenance union** (facts.go:310–333): Keeps anchors from both, dedupes by (SessionID, Commit, CheckpointID, TurnID, Transcript, Line).

---

### 5. Determinism & Cost

**Token spending**: Distill *always* calls the model (one call per chunk, one per reconciliation). Not deterministic-only—every chunk without a cache hit triggers an agent call.

**Deterministic path**: Fingerprint + cache. If session fingerprint matches and not `--force`, zero agent calls for that session (cache hit). No deterministic-only extraction mode (unlike some "patterns" features that might be).

**Failure handling**:
- Agent call failure: chunk skipped, fact lines dropped, session not cached (retried next run)
- Failure streak (5+ with no success): aborted with error (misconfiguration detected)
- Reconcile agent failure: all candidates treated as `new` (facts retained, no merge/supersede applied)
- Midrun write failure: non-fatal, retried next interval; doesn't abort the run
- Partial output: capped at 6/chunk; extras silently dropped with warning

**Cost model**: Deterministic on identity, token-heavy on extraction and reconciliation. `--dry-run` estimates without agent calls. `--concurrency` pools extraction calls; reconcile calls are serial (one per chunk with candidates).

---

### 6. Distill ↔ Refresh Integration

**Not integrated**: Distill is a separate, manual/opt-in command (`entire brain distill`). Refresh does NOT call distill. They are independent pipelines:
- **Refresh**: exports sessions, builds seed/history/semantic indexes, updates manifest
- **Distill**: reads exported sessions, synthesizes facts, updates fact store independently

**Gating**:
- No env vars, no automatic triggers
- User runs `entire brain distill` manually after (or before) `refresh`
- Manifest integration: both read/write the same manifest file, but distill is orthogonal to refresh's session/seed/history/semantic flows

---

### 7. Provenance & Anchoring

**factAnchor structure** (facts.go:106–114):
```go
type factAnchor struct {
    SessionID    string // required: which session
    Commit       string // optional: commit SHA if available
    CheckpointID string // optional: the checkpoint this turn was in
    TurnID       string // optional: turn-level ID (Phase B)
    Transcript   string // brain-relative path to transcript file
    Line         int    // 1-based line number in transcript (chunk.StartLine)
    Verified     bool   // signed-source metadata
}
```

**Computation** (distill_cmd.go:873–878):
```go
anchor := factAnchor{
    SessionID:    session.SessionID,
    CheckpointID: session.LatestCheckpoint,
    Transcript:   filepath.ToSlash(session.TranscriptPath),
    Line:         chunk.StartLine, // 1-based line offset from preprocessing
}
```

**Multiple anchors**: A fact may accumulate anchors across re-distills (upsert unions them). Reconcile preserves all prior anchors.

---

## Key Function Signatures & File Locations

| Function | File:Line | Signature |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| `newDistillCommand` | distill_cmd.go:473 | `func(opts Options) *cobra.Command` |
| `runDistill` | distill_cmd.go:506 | `func(ctx Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, distillOpts distillCommandOptions, target string) error` |
| `runDistillForBrain` | distill_cmd.go:612 | `func(ctx Context, repoDir, brainDir string, distillOpts distillCommandOptions, now time.Time) (*factSourceManifest, error)` |
| `startSessionPrefetch` | distill_cmd.go:159 | `func(ctx Context, brainDir, repoDir string, args []string, sessions []exportSession, prevCache distillCache, distillOpts distillCommandOptions, resolveBranch func(exportSession) string) <-chan preparedSession` |
| `distilledFactsFromOutput` | distill.go:192 | `func(output string, taxonomy factTaxonomy, anchor factAnchor, branch string, now time.Time) ([]factRecord, []string)` |
| `reconcileChunkCandidates` | reconcile.go:308 | `func(ctx Context, run distillAgentRunner, agentArgs []string, candidates, active []factRecord, repoDir string, timeout time.Duration) ([]factAction, []string)` |
| `applyFactActions` | facts_merge.go:58 | `func(active []factRecord, actions []factAction, threshold float64, now time.Time) ([]factRecord, []factProposal)` |
| `upsertFact` | facts.go:287 | `func(records []factRecord, incoming factRecord) []factRecord` |
| `inferFactKind` | facts_locus.go:127 | `func(paths []string, text string) string` |
| `factLocus` | facts_locus.go:245 | `func(text string) []string` |
| `renderDistillPrompt` | distill.go:57 | `func(taxonomy factTaxonomy) (string, error)` |
| `distillAgentCommandArgs` | distill.go:105 | `func(agent string, agentCommand []string, prompt string) ([]string, error)` |

---

## Architecture Patterns for Your "Patterns" Feature

**Reusable abstractions you should mirror**:

1. **Session prefetch pipeline** (startSessionPrefetch): Two-stage goroutine producer—prep + global dispatch—decouples work-lookahead from pool concurrency. Critical for not starving the pool on skip/cache-heavy regions.
